pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty HIGH: API Gateway prod (us-west) is seeing a spike in 502/504 responses — 14% 5xx over last 3m. Alerting SRE oncall.

sre-oncall-jordan: acked — I'm on it. @emily-mlinfra @raj-api can you join the triage?

emily-mlinfra: on my way. pulling up graphs (p95 latency, upstream timeouts).

emily-mlinfra: quick snapshot from grafana: gateway p95 = 1.2s, 5xx rate = 14%, request rate unchanged. upstream model-service latencies spiking; tail latencies > 3s.

raj-api: I'm seeing a surge of Envoy 504s in the ingress pods: "upstream request timeout" repeated. Also some connection reset by peer in the logs.

sre-oncall-jordan: likely upstream slowness or connection pool exhaustion. Are we hitting any deployment rollouts recently?

emily-mlinfra: no deploys in last 30m. Running `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=model-service -o wide` shows 6/10 ready across nodepool-3. nodepool-3 nodes show high CPU (90%).

raj-api: attaching a small log snippet from envoy on in-proxy: ```
[2026-11-02T15:34:01Z] "POST /v1/generate" 504 Upstream request timeout via ingress-cluster (upstream_host: 10.2.3.45:8080)
[2026-11-02T15:34:02Z] "POST /v1/generate" 502 Bad Gateway (connection reset)
```

emily-mlinfra: running `kubectl logs -n prod model-service-7bb9 -c model --tail 200` shows worker threads blocking on KV cache fetches and long GC cycles in python layer. Could be memory pressure + GC pauses leading to slow responses.

ops-shift-lead: customer-impact estimate? any billing or critical customers affected?

product-support: seeing multiple customer tickets about timeouts — appears to affect mid-to-large request payloads (longer seq lengths). Roughly 12 customers reported in last 20m.

sre-oncall-jordan: immediate mitigations: 1) enable fail-open routing to smaller-model variant for requests exceeding 1k tokens, 2) rate-limit /v1/generate per API key at edge to 10rps burst 20, 3) add temporary autoscale to model-service replicas. Will coordinate.

emily-mlinfra: applying autoscale: `kubectl scale deploy model-service --replicas=12 -n prod` — command run.

raj-api: can we patch Envoy route to reduce max connections to upstream and increase timeout? I want to avoid saturating the model pool. Proposed: set timeout to 15s (was 30s), max_connections 150 per upstream.

sre-oncall-jordan: do it, and also push routing weight to fallback-model variant at 30% for canary.

deploy-bot: canary route-change applied to 30% of traffic for fallback-model.

emily-mlinfra: model-service replicas scaling triggered, pods starting. Watching readiness.

raj-api: envoys updated with new connection limits. Confirming no crash loops from envoy.

(reacts: :thumbsup: by emily-mlinfra, :eyes: by product-support)

sre-oncall-jordan: rate limit rules applied at edge for /v1/generate — per-key 10rps, global 1500rps.

emily-mlinfra: after scaling and routing change, 5xx rate dropped to 4% in last 2m. p95 latency down to 420ms. Still seeing occasional 502s from nodepool-3.

raj-api: digging into nodepool-3 nodes — one node has flapping kubelet, causing pod churn. Ops to cordon and drain that node.

ops-shift-lead: cordon node np3-12, draining pods. Starting replacement node.

product-support: notifying impacted customers with templated message: "We're investigating intermittent timeouts, mitigation in flight; expect updates in 30 minutes."

emily-mlinfra: GC tuning change prepared as hotfix for model container (reduce max heap fragmentation). Will rollout to 2 pods first.

sre-oncall-jordan: proceed with canary GC tune on two model pods. Monitor for improvements.

(10 minutes pass)

emily-mlinfra: canary GC change showed improved worker stability; no blocking on KV fetches observed on those pods.

raj-api: after draining np3-12 and scaling, 5xx rate now 0.9% and p95 200ms. Deploy-bot confirms canary routing remains at 30% fallback.

sre-oncall-jordan: looks like this is mitigated. Keeping incident open for postmortem items: nodepool health checks, GC defaults, autoscale thresholds, and better circuit-breaker defaults at Envoy.

product-support: updating customers: "Issue mitigated; we're monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause in a postmortem."

ops-shift-lead: handing off to night oncall. @sre-oncall-jordan please summarize for handoff.

sre-oncall-jordan: handoff summary: 502/504 spike caused by combination of nodepool kubelet flapping and model-service GC/backpressure leading to upstream timeouts. Immediate mitigations: scaled model-service, cordoned/drained bad node, applied rate-limits at edge, shifted 30% traffic to fallback-model variant, tuned GC in canary pods, lowered Envoy upstream timeout and connection limits. Current state: stabilized (5xx <1%), monitoring for 1h. Follow-ups: postmortem, revise autoscale thresholds, add healthcheck alert for nodepool kubelet jitter, consider preemptive fallback routing for long-sequence requests.

(reacts: :white_check_mark: by product-support)

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged as HIGH; marked Resolved by oncall after stabilization. Please file postmortem and tag #incidents.

sre-oncall-jordan: filing postmortem now (will link here when ready). Good handoff.

emily-mlinfra: added a note to runbooks about temporary rate-limits and model-variant fallback.

product-support: will follow up with impacted customers tomorrow with the postmortem link.

end of thread.
